title: Proper-support shrinking for an inverse-ring local model
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$, and put $X_0=|X_1|\subseteq|X|$, the common underlying closed subset of all the $X_n$. Let $W\subseteq X$ be an open subspace containing $X_0$, and let $F$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module. Assume that its pullback $F\otimes_A A_1$ to $X_1$ has support proper over $A_1$. There exists an open subspace $W'\subseteq W$ containing $X_0$ such that $F|_{W'}$ has support proper over $A$.

proof.text: Put $I=\ker(A\to A_1)$. Apply [lem-sfb-nil-ring-tower-limit-henselian] to obtain $A/I\simeq A_1$ and the henselian pair $(A,I)$. Thus the special base for the proper-part lifting theorem is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}A_1$.

First replace $W$ by a quasi-compact open $W_0$ with $X_0\subseteq W_0\subseteq W$. Indeed $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact, and [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] shows that $X_1$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] to the identity of $X_1$ to identify this with topological quasi-compactness. Take an etale scheme atlas of $W$ and cover it by affine opens. By the same open-image lemma their images are quasi-compact open subspaces covering $W$. Their intersections with $X_0$ cover the quasi-compact point space of $X_1$; choose finitely many and let $W_0$ be their union. The empty union is allowed. Restriction to an open preserves local finite type, since on affine chart neighborhoods it is localization of a finitely generated algebra; hence $W_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is of finite type. Its relative diagonal is the restriction of that of $X$, so it is separated.

Write $M=F|_{W_0}$. It is finite type because its finite presentation supplies finitely many generators. By [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] its quasi-coherent annihilator defines a closed subspace $Z\hookrightarrow W_0$. Its point set is $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$: on any affine etale chart a finite set of module generators vanishes at a prime precisely when their annihilator contains an element outside that prime (multiply the finitely many denominators killing the generators). This is also the geometric-stalk support by [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support]. The closed immersion is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], so is finite type; [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition] makes $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ finite type. It is separated: after every scheme test the diagonal of $Z/A$ is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $W_0/A$.

Put $Z_0=Z\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_1$. Its point set inside $X_1$ is $\operatorname{Supp}(F\otimes_A A_1)$: the fibre-product point-image formula in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identifies it with the inverse image of $|Z|$, and [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback] identifies that inverse image with the support of the tensor pullback. Here $W_0\times_X X_1=X_1$, since its image lies in $W_0$. By the hypothesis and [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support], the annihilator support of $F\otimes_A A_1$ is proper over $A_1$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] on $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1$: any closed subspace with that same point set is proper, so $Z_0$ is proper. The local-finite-type hypothesis holds on charts by tensoring finite algebra generators with $A_1$. This uses equality of point sets, not equality of annihilator subschemes.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-henselian-proper-clopen-lift] to the separated finite-type space $Z/A$, the pair $(A,I)$, and the whole special fibre $Z_0$ (open and closed in itself). It gives an open and closed subspace $Z_1\subseteq Z$ proper over $A$ whose special fibre is all of $Z_0$. Write $Z_2=Z\setminus Z_1$. It is closed in $Z$, hence closed in $W_0$, and its point set is disjoint from $X_0$, because its special fibre is empty.

source.place: Tag 0CWI (lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian), with Y equal to the entire special fibre.

proof.text: Take $W^{\prime}=W_0\setminus|Z_2|$. It is open, contains $X_0$, and is contained in the original $W$. The support of $F|_{W^{\prime}}$ is $|Z_1|$ by [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback] for the open inclusion. More precisely its annihilator support is $Z\times_{W_0}W^{\prime}=Z_1$: annihilating local sections commutes with restriction to an open. Since $Z_1$ is proper over $A$, [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] gives proper support in exactly the closed-carrier sense of the statement.

Live still has the item unsplit with the same statement. There is no repair note, so this is not a re-split, and no live or side-live node states 0CT7. The item abstracts exactly what the 0CXA proof uses. Proper support is handled through equal point sets plus 0CZC: any closed subspace with the same point set is proper. This avoids the source's claim that annihilators commute with non-flat base change, which is false (k[x,y] example: (t^2) vs (t)). The new node is 0CT7 for an N-indexed tower, statement only, with 6 Mathlib searches recorded. IsAdicComplete.henselianRing needs adic completeness, so it is not a match. The node is true on Z/p^n, a constant tower and k[t]/t^n, and is not a duplicate. Step checks: (1) henselian pair (A,I) with A/I = A_1. (2) The finite subcover gives a quasi-compact open W_0 inside W even when W is not quasi-compact; W_0 -> Spec A is quasi-compact by two elementary lines through the affine atlas pieces. (3) Annihilator closed subspace Z with |Z| = Supp; Z is finite type (04XZ, 03XG) and separated. (4) Z_0 has point set Supp(F tensor A_1) (03H4, 07TZ(3)) and is proper by the carrier-support lemma and 0CZC. (5) 0CWI hypotheses all hold; Z_2 misses X_0. (6) W' = W_0 minus Z_2 gives annihilator support Z_1, which is proper.
